tool_input.command: echo "# Tool call log" > calllog.md && echo "1. Skill excalidraw-skill (loaded)" >> calllog.md && npx -y mcp-excalidraw-server status --url http://127.0.0.1:4732; echo "exit=$?"; echo "2. Bash: status --url :4732" >> calllog.md
tool_input.description: Start log and check canvas server status

result:
The figure is on the canvas at http://127.0.0.1:4732, and the last screenshot (`shot3.png`) passes every check. The call-by-call log is in `calllog.md`.

**(1) Calls and screenshots**
- **Calls:** 20 tool calls in total, and 2 of them were blocked by a hook ("elkdraw-eval: not allowlisted"). One was a command chained with `&&`, the other used a pipe. After that I ran single commands only.
- **Canvas commands:** 9 CLI commands ran against the canvas: `status`, `add` (65 elements), `query`, `describe`, two `apply` patches and three `screenshot`s.
- **Screenshots:** I took 3 and looked at each one.
  - `shot1.png` had three bugs:
    - The whole tree sat 22px to the left of the array. That was my mistake: I used each node's centre as its x position.
    - Nodes "12" and "10" wrapped onto two lines.
    - The index labels were left-aligned, even though I had set them to centre.
  - `shot2.png` fixed the tree, but my workaround made the index and lo/hi labels invisible.
  - `shot3.png` is the final version.

**(2) How I checked**
- **Alignment:**
  - **By numbers:** column i is centred at x = 108 + 60·i. Tree node k is placed at column k−1, which is its position in the in-order array. `describe` confirms the stored positions, e.g. node 11 at x=682, width 52, centre 708, and cell 10 at x=680, width 56, centre 708.
  - **By eye:** node centres in `shot3` line up with the cells below them (1 over 1, 11 over 11, 15 over 15). The lo arrow is under the cell holding 9 (index 8), and the hi arrow is under the cell holding 12 (index 11).
  - **Limit:** the index labels were placed by guessing glyph widths, not measured. The server doesn't store the width the browser actually renders, so their centring is only as good as my eye on the screenshot. Any error there is a pixel or two.
- **Highlight:** checked by eye. The nodes 8, 12, 10 and 11, and the three edges between them, are the only red, thick-bordered items in the tree. The cell for 11 is tinted red too, which is an extra I added.
- **14px text:** the screenshot comes back at about 1:1 scale, so 14px text is roughly 14 screen pixels tall. I can read every index label, 0 to 14, and the array title "in-order array A[0..14]". But they are small, grey and in a hand-drawn font. I'm confident about the digits, not about fine detail. For example, a label 1px off, or a smudged stroke, would get past me. I had no way to zoom through the CLI, so this was a squint check, not a close inspection.

**(3) Worst moment**
The fix after the first screenshot. The server reported my index labels as 56px wide and centred, but the browser drew them left-aligned. So I put the labels inside invisible rectangles, since container labels do centre. The CLI accepted all 17 without complaint, and the next screenshot showed that every index label and both lo/hi labels had disappeared. The text had silently taken on the rectangles' transparent colour, and the tool has no way to colour a label separately. That cost a full round and forced me back to placing text by guessed glyph widths.

Separately, the hook blocking `&&` and pipes meant I kept the log with file writes instead of shell appends.

Files are in /private/tmp/audit-p1-bst-a.WQLj:
- shot1.png
- shot2.png
- shot3.png
- calllog.md
